title: Nicla recovery reports only 0x0607, which the ground ignores: the Nicla stays "lost" on the ground and the separation alarm is dropped
description: When the Nicla canary trips (aru_fail_count_ > 5) the flight sends 0x0606 "Nicla Sense ME stopped responding on <bus>", and the ground's SensorBusState marks the Nicla "lost". When the Nicla answers again, the flight only sends 0x0607 "Nicla Sense ME responding again" (flight.cpp:1996-1998). aru_.ok() never goes false, so probe_nicla() and its 0x060B acquisition report never run again. 0x0607 is not in dictionary.SENSOR_BUS_EVRS, and SensorBusState.on_evr (sensors.py:296-323) returns False for it. The RM3100 path is different: it re-reports through 0x060B.
failure_scenario: I reproduced this with the real SensorBusState. Nicla and RM3100 outboard both on A4/A5, so the 0x060D "not separated" EVR arrives and separated() is False (YELLOW alarm). Then the ESLOV wire bounces: 0x0606, then 0x0607 a few seconds later. Result: snapshot separated=None, text "unknown (no current acquisition report of the Nicla Sense ME)", Nicla state "lost", lost=['Nicla Sense ME (A4/A5)'], although HK NICLA_ME is set again. The wiring is still wrong but the YELLOW reason disappears until the next reboot.
proposed_fix: Flight: in the 0x0607 branch call report_acquired("Nicla Sense ME", aru_bus_, SBUS_NICLA) and report_separation(u) for both units. Alternatively, on the ground, treat 0x0607 as a re-acquisition on the Nicla's last reported bus. Add an e2e test for the drop/return sequence.
verifier_evidence: NiclaAru::ok() is set only in begin() (payload.cpp:10, payload.h:53), so after a canary trip aru_.ok() stays true and reprobe_instruments() never calls probe_nicla() again (flight.cpp:2043). The reads simply resume in start_mag_sample, which sets SNS_NICLA_ME again (flight.cpp:2303), and fdir_1hz only sends INFO 0x0607 (flight.cpp:1996-1998). 0x0607 is not in dictionary.SENSOR_BUS_EVRS (dictionary.py:147-156), and SensorBusState.on_evr returns False for it. I reproduced the finding with the real module (verify-FL/fl01.py). Boot reports put the Nicla and the ob unit both on A4/A5 with WARN 0x060D 'not separated', and separated() is False. After 0x0606 then 0x0607, on_evr(0x0607) is False and the snapshot is separated=None, 'unknown (no current acquisition report of the Nicla Sense ME)', nicla state 'lost', lost=['Nicla Sense ME (A4/A5)'], with HK all OK. The YELLOW reason (gds.py:2160) is gone until the next reboot. The Nicla also shows 'lost' in every layout after any outage longer than 6 s. tests/test_sensors.py:225 models the recovery as a 0x060B, which the flight never sends for the Nicla.
verifier_fix_notes: Simplest fix, ground only: in SensorBusState.on_evr, treat 0x0607 'Nicla Sense ME responding again' as a re-acquisition on the Nicla's last reported bus. Keep the playback rule. Add the format to SENSOR_BUS_EVRS (the cross-check test covers it). The pair verdict then becomes False again from the stored RM3100 bus and the YELLOW returns. Change test_lost_instruments_and_recovery to feed 0x0607. Flight-side alternative: in the 0x0607 branch call report_acquired("Nicla Sense ME", aru_bus_, SBUS_NICLA) and report_separation(0/1). This costs extra VC0 EVRs (see FL-07).

title: MAG-bus FDIR can never fire when only RM3100s are on it: loss detection stops traffic at <= 10 consecutive errors, the FDIR threshold is > 10
description: Each failed RM3100 sample adds one consecutive error (the POLL write8 fails, I2cBus::note(false)). note_mag_sample marks the unit lost after kRm3100LossSamples = 5 failures, and after that it is never polled. That is 5 consecutive errors with one unit and exactly 10 with two. fdir_1hz recovers a bus only when consecutive_errors() > kI2cFdirErrors (10) (flight.cpp:1968). The re-probe path adds nothing: I2cBus::probe() is not counted, and Rm3100::begin stops at the failed probe. bus_clear_failed_[SBUS_MAG] is always false because recover() returns true without pins. So the MAG bus is never re-initialised (the PE reset in setClock). In 3.0 the RM3100s shared the bus with the Nicla, which is polled every second, so the count went past 10 and the bus was recovered.
failure_scenario: Recommended layout (RM3100 ob, optionally ib, alone on Qwiic; AS7265X on A4/A5). The I2C4 controller locks up after a glitch on the long boom cable, and every transfer fails. The RM3100 is declared lost after 5 s (0x060E) with consec_ = 5 (or 10). No 0x0605, no FDIR_I2C_BUS and no recover() ever follow. Re-probes every 30 s to 10 min fail on the stuck controller, so the boom magnetometers stay lost until a reboot. FDIR only works in the owner's layout because the AS7265X FAULT path happens to share the bus.
proposed_fix: In note_mag_sample when a unit is declared lost, or in reprobe_instruments before probing a lost unit, call bus_recover(b, now, "RM3100 lost") on mag_bus_of_[u] when recover_[b].allowed() and bus_of(b).consecutive_errors() > 0. Alternatively, make the FDIR trigger reachable, e.g. >= kRm3100LossSamples on a bus whose only instruments were declared lost.
verifier_evidence: The mechanism is right. Rm3100::start() makes one counted write8 per sample (sensors.cpp:41), and I2cBus::note(false) adds one consecutive error (i2c_bus.cpp:20-24). probe() is not counted (i2c_bus.cpp:26-29), and begin() stops at the failed probe. note_mag_sample marks the unit lost at kRm3100LossSamples=5 (sensor_bus.h:70, flight.cpp:2322-2331). After that, start_mag_sample skips it (want = en && m.ok()). fdir_1hz needs consecutive_errors() > 10 (flight.cpp:87, 1968). I modelled it with the real LossCounter (verify-FL/fl02.cpp): the maximum is 5 consecutive errors with one unit and 10 with two, and FDIR fires for 0 s per hour. bus_clear_failed_[SBUS_MAG] is always false (recover() returns true without pins). So with only RM3100s on Qwiic (the contract section 3 layout), 0x0605, FDIR_I2C_BUS and recover() never happen. The consequence is overstated, though: 'stays lost until reboot' is not supported. The Zephyr 0.90 STM32 v2 driver calls LL_I2C_Disable (PE=0, the same block reset that setClock gives) in i2c_stm32_master_mode_end at the end of every transfer: STOP, NACK->STOP, error and timeout paths, i2c_ll_stm32_v2.c:269-288, 619, 659, 692-693. It also re-enables PE in msg_init (line 233). A controller-state lockup that recover() would clear is therefore already cleared on every transfer, and the 30 s-10 min re-probes keep running. A target holding SDA cannot be fixed on Qwiic either way. The real loss is the missing 0x0605/I2C_BUS report and an unreachable per-bus FDIR path.
verifier_fix_notes: In note_mag_sample, when a unit is declared lost and bus_of(mag_bus_of_[unit]).consecutive_errors() >= kRm3100LossSamples (the errors are bus-wide), set FDIR_I2C_BUS, send 0x0605 and call bus_recover(b, millis(), "RM3100 lost") if recover_[b].allowed(). Gate this on fdir_mask_ & FDIR_I2C_BUS. Or document that on a Qwiic bus holding only RM3100s, the loss EVR 0x060E replaces the bus FDIR. Also correct the i2c_bus.h claim that setClock is the only controller reset: the driver already toggles PE on every transfer.

title: Page 2 is read only in PA-off windows: about 31 % of the ARU's 1 s windows are never aggregated and IMU_F_GAP is set in almost every ATT
description: The ARU publishes only the last completed 1.000 s window. The flight reads page 2 only inside the 1 Hz magnetometer sample, which waits in MAG_WAIT while tx_state_ != TX_IDLE. In TEST/ENCOUNTER the E22 at 2.4 kbit/s is busy 1267 ms of every 2534 ms frame period, so reads are delayed by up to 1.27 s. Whenever two windows close between two reads, the older one is lost: ImuStats counts it as a gap and leaves it out of vib_rms, vib_peak, rate_mean and rate_peak. docs/13 9.4 describes imu_nwin as "1 s windows in the ATT period" and rate_peak as "the largest |omega| of one sample in the period". In practice they cover only the windows that happened to be read. GAP (amber on the dashboard) can no longer tell an ARU that misses samples apart from normal transmitting.
failure_scenario: I simulated it: 1 Hz due samples deferred to the end of 1.267 s TX bursts every 2.534 s, with random Nicla window phase, over 200 h. Only 68.7 % of windows were read, and 97.2 % of 8 s TEST ATT periods carry IMU_F_GAP. A 1 s motion event (peak rate above still_rate_dps) falls in an unread window about 31 % of the time, and the ground then shows "stationary" for that ATT period.
proposed_fix: Read page 2 every second regardless of the PA. It is a read of statistics already computed on the Nicla; the PA-off rule protects the magnetometer samples, and page 2 has none. Keep the paired page-0/page-2 read inside the sample for q_grv/IMU_F_PAIRED. Alternatively, have the ARU keep cumulative sums (count, sum of vib_rms^2, max peaks, sum of rate means) since boot, so the flight can difference them without losing windows. Report flight-side skips separately from ARU_IMU_MISSED, or fix the docs/13 wording.
verifier_evidence: service_mag waits in MAG_WAIT while tx_state_ != TX_IDLE (flight.cpp:2232). Page 2 is read only inside start_mag_sample (flight.cpp:2280), and the ARU exposes only the last completed window (nicla_sense_me_aru.ino close_window/g_win, page rebuild at 10 Hz). ENCOUNTER/TEST frame period = 2.0 x busy (datalink.cpp:284). Busy = 236 octets: 246 ms UART + 1023 ms air at 2.4 kbit/s = ~1268 ms (radio.cpp:122-127). TX start is not held back by MAG_WAIT (flight.cpp:963-965 holds only MAG_COLLECT). My Monte Carlo (verify-FL/fl03.py, 50 h, 1 Hz ticks deferred to TX end, random Nicla phase, 20 ppm drift, 0-100 ms rebuild latency) gives windows read 69.2 % in TEST/ENCOUNTER, 75 % in CRUISE and 84 % in SAFE. 97 % of 8 s ATT periods (100 % of 60 s CRUISE periods) contain an unread window, so IMU_F_GAP is effectively always amber and no longer separates ARU_IMU_MISSED from normal transmitting. docs/13 9.4 ('1 s windows in the ATT period', rate_peak 'the largest |omega| of one sample in the period') overstates what is aggregated. The design comment (attitude.h:91-93) knowingly accepts unread windows, but not at this rate. One correction: read gaps never exceed ~1.27 s, so two consecutive windows are never both unread. A sustained 1 s motion at random phase therefore almost always reaches a read window. The ~31 % miss rate applies to sub-second impulses that fall inside one window, not to every 1 s motion.
verifier_fix_notes: Read page 2 (one ~3 ms transfer on the NICLA bus) once per second independent of the PA. The PA-off rule protects RM3100 samples, and AS7265X polling already runs during TX with a budget. Keep the paired page-0/page-2 read in the sample for q_grv/IMU_F_PAIRED, and feed imu_stats_ from whichever read is newer (win_seq de-dup already handles duplicates). Alternative: cumulative window sums on the ARU. At minimum, fix the docs/13 wording and report flight-side skips separately from ARU_IMU_MISSED.

title: ImuStats keeps accumulating while ATT is off (SAFE): the first ATT after SAFE carries hours of windows
description: imu_stats_.add() runs at every 1 Hz sample in every mode, but reset() is called only in gen_att(). ATT cadence is 0 in BOOT and SAFE (datalink.cpp kModeCadence) and when a period override switches ATT off. The spacecraft boots into SAFE and stays there until the ground commands a mode. The first ATT afterwards therefore aggregates everything since boot: imu_nwin saturates at 255, vib_peak and rate_peak are maxima over hours, and gap_/acc_sat_ are latched from any moment in that time.
failure_scenario: Boot, then 2 h in SAFE with the spacecraft handled once (a 3 deg/s bump), then CRUISE. The first ATT (60 s period) shows imu_nwin 255, rate_peak 3.0 deg/s and GAP, so the ground shows "moving" for a spacecraft that has been still for 2 h. The IMU time chart plots that period as one point.
proposed_fix: Reset imu_stats_ when ATT is not being generated, e.g. in tick_1hz: if (stretched ATT period == 0) imu_stats_.reset(); or reset it on every set_mode(). Optionally do the same for mstat_* (pre-existing).
verifier_evidence: imu_stats_.add() runs at every successful 1 Hz sample in every mode (flight.cpp:2290), and reset() is called only in gen_att() (flight.cpp:1869; that is the only reset site). ATT cadence is 0 in BOOT and SAFE (datalink.cpp:277-278) and with a 0xFFFF override (flight.cpp:1565), and tick_1hz skips period 0 (flight.cpp:1600). setup() enters SAFE (flight.cpp:319). set_mode() zeroes last_gen_s_ (flight.cpp:1152), so the first ATT after SAFE->CRUISE is generated at the next tick and carries everything since boot: windows() saturates at 255 (attitude.h:104), the peaks are maxima over hours, and gap_/acc_sat_/gyro_sat_ are latched. A 3 deg/s bump hours earlier gives rate_peak 3.0 > still_rate_dps 0.5, i.e. 'moving'.
verifier_fix_notes: In tick_1hz, call imu_stats_.reset() when the stretched ATT period is 0. reset() keeps seen_/last_win_, so nothing is double counted. Or reset it in set_mode(). Optionally do the same for mstat_ob_/ib_/body_ (MAG off in SAFE, pre-existing).

title: MAG packet after a run-time RM3100 loss: the OB/IB flag is set but the vector is the sentinel, and the period's valid samples are discarded
description: Before 3.1, Rm3100::ok() could not go false at run time. Now note_mag_sample() calls mark_lost(). gen_mag sets MAG_F_OB/IB from mstat_*.count() != 0 but fills the vector with mag_vec(mstat_ob_, mag_ob_.ok()). For a unit lost during the MAG period, ok() is false, so the field is 0x7FFFFFFF n/a while the flag says "OB ok". rm3100_cycle_count also switches to the inboard unit.
failure_scenario: CRUISE (MAG period 30 s): the outboard RM3100 gives 20 good samples, then its cable is pulled and it is declared lost after 5 more (0x060E) before gen_mag runs. MAG flags b1 OB = 1, nsamples = 20, but ob_bx/by/bz/rms decode to None: 20 valid measurements are dropped and the packet contradicts itself.
proposed_fix: Use the accumulator alone: p.outboard = mag_vec(mstat_ob_, true) (count() == 0 already yields the sentinels), and likewise for inboard. Take rm3100_cycle_count from the cycle count in force (mag_cc_) instead of ok().
verifier_evidence: Rm3100::mark_lost() sets ok_=false at run time (sensors.h mark_lost, called from note_mag_sample flight.cpp:2325). gen_mag sets MAG_F_OB/IB from mstat_*.count() != 0 but builds the vector with mag_vec(mstat_ob_, mag_ob_.ok()) (flight.cpp:1764-1769), and mag_vec returns the sentinels when !ok (flight.cpp:249-251). Samples added before the loss are valid: finish_mag_unit adds only ok samples (flight.cpp:2340-2345). So a unit lost inside a MAG period gives OB=1 and nsamples>0 with ob_bx..rms = n/a. rm3100_cycle_count switches to mag_ib_.cycle_count() (flight.cpp:1771). For an unfitted ib that is its default cc_=200 (sensors.h), not the commanded mag_cc_.
verifier_fix_notes: Use p.outboard = mag_vec(mstat_ob_, true) and p.inboard = mag_vec(mstat_ib_, true). count()==0 already yields the sentinels, and the ok guard dates from 3.0, when ok() was constant. Report rm3100_cycle_count = mag_cc_ (the cycle count in force).

title: An ARU restart is not flagged as a gap, contrary to the comment and to what the host test claims
description: attitude.cpp:314-315 says that a counter moving backwards (an ARU restart) shows as a gap. A rebooted Nicla serves page 2 with win_seq 0, n 0 and flags b5|b6 only for about 1 s before its first window (Wire.begin comes after the 1 s setup delay, and g_win_t0 starts there). The special case at line 309 takes that page silently (seen_ = true, last_win_ = 0), and the next window (win_seq 1) is consecutive. The windows lost during the reboot never set IMU_F_GAP. test_sensor_bus.cpp:143 ("a jump (ARU restart) is a gap") tests 0 -> 200, which is not the sequence a restart produces.
failure_scenario: I checked this with a host program against attitude.cpp: add(99), add(100), [Nicla power-cycles, reads fail about 2 s], add(win_seq 0, n 0, flags 0x60), add(1). Result: gap()=0, windows()=3. The ATT for that period shows no GAP although 3 or more windows are missing.
proposed_fix: In the win_seq 0 / n 0 branch set gap_ = true when seen_ && last_win_ != 0 (a counter that went back to the pre-first-window state). Change the host test to feed the real restart sequence (..., 100, {0, n 0, flags 0x60}, 1) and expect gap().
verifier_evidence: The ARU firmware starts the I2C target (Wire.begin) right before g_win_t0 = millis() (nicla_sense_me_aru.ino:339-342). For the first ~1 s after a restart, page 2 therefore carries win_seq 0, n 0, flags GRV_PRESENT|ACC_RANGE (0x60/0x61, no STATS/MISSED). ImuStats::add takes that through the special case (attitude.cpp:184-188) without a gap and sets last_win_=0, so the next window 1 is consecutive. I built a host program against the real attitude.cpp (verify-FL/fl06.cpp): add(99), add(100), add({0,n0,0x60}), add(1) gives gap=0, windows=3. Only when the first post-restart read is already window 1 does gap become 1. The comment at attitude.cpp:189-190 ('an ARU restart also shows as a gap') and the host test 'a jump (ARU restart) is a gap' (test_sensor_bus.cpp, 0 -> 200) do not match the real restart sequence. Practical impact is low while FL-03 keeps GAP almost always set.
verifier_fix_notes: In the win_seq 0 / n 0 branch, add 'if (seen_ && last_win_ != 0) gap_ = true;' before last_win_ = 0. Make the host test feed ..., 100, {0, n 0, flags 0x60}, 1 and expect gap(). Keep the first-boot case (seen_ false) gap-free.

title: New boot-time 0x060B/0x060D EVRs fill the VC0 routine budget, so later boot INFO EVRs (BOOT, BIST, station ID) are refused on the real-time downlink
description: All boot EVRs are queued on VC0 during setup(), with nothing transmitted until loop() starts. A non-priority packet is refused once backlog + len > 1024 - 256 = 768 octets (datalink.cpp:66); a priority WARN can use the reserve but still adds to the backlog. 3.1 adds one 0x060B per instrument at boot (~60 octets each) and, for a wrong-bus or not-separated wiring, two WARN 0x060D per RM3100 (~85-88 octets each). My estimate for a normal boot with both RM3100s on Qwiic is ~760 of the 768 octets.
failure_scenario: Nicla plus RM3100 ob and ib all on A4/A5. That is the wiring docs/03 still describes, and the boot emits 2 x (0x060B + two 0x060D). Cumulative VC0 is about 756 octets after the sensor EVRs, so the INFO BIST results 0x0910/0x0911, "BOOT VGQ-1 FSW 3.1 rst=...", 0x0003, 0x0004 and "DE <callsign>" are all refused in real time (Downlink overflows counted) and exist only in the SSR. With a single wrong-bus RM3100, 0x0004 and the station ID are lost.
proposed_fix: Emit the BOOT EVR before init_sensors(), or send the setup-time EVRs with priority=true (or exempt in_setup_ from the routine reserve). Alternatively, fold the per-instrument acquisition into one boot EVR (e.g. "buses: Nicla A4/A5, ob Qwiic, ib Qwiic, AS7265X Qwiic") that the ground parses.
verifier_evidence: Nothing is transmitted during setup(). evr() pushes INFO EVRs as non-priority (flight.cpp:1556), and Downlink::push refuses them once backlog + len > 1024 - 256 (datalink.cpp:66-75). WARNs use the reserve but still add to the backlog. in_setup_ exempts only the EvrGate, not the VC limit (flight.cpp:1553). An EVR packet is 15 + text octets (pack_evr, 6+6 headers). I summed the literal boot formats in order (verify-FL/fl07.py): 0x0308, 0x0306, the 0x060B/0x060D sensor reports, 0x0910/0x0911, 0x0706, MODE 0x0011, BOOT 0x0001, 0x0003, 0x0004, 0x0002. Results: (a) Nicla, ob and ib all on A4/A5 (the layout docs/03 still shows, lines 71/89/133): 687 octets after the sensor EVRs. 0x0911, 0x0706, MODE, BOOT, 0x0003, 0x0004 and 'DE N0CALL' are refused in real time. (b) One RM3100 on A4/A5: 0x0003, 0x0004 and DE are refused. (c) Even the normal 3.1 boot with ob+ib on Qwiic comes to ~758-782 octets, so 0x0004 (strap fitted) or the station-ID EVR (no strap) is refused, which is slightly worse than the reviewer's ~760. The 3.0 equivalent without the 0x060B reports came to ~615. All are still in the SSR and the EGSE log. BOOT 0x0001 is not used by ground logic (dictionary.py:162 only), and the callsign is also sent every 600 s and in the idle frames, so the impact is minor.
verifier_fix_notes: Emit BOOT/0x0003/0x0004/0x0002 right after init_radio(), before init_sensors(). In report_acquired, send either 0x060B (preferred bus) or the wrong-bus 0x060D, not both: the ground already reads 0x060D as an acquisition (dictionary.evr_instrument_bus). Optionally let setup-time EVRs use the priority reserve (in_setup_ -> priority). Re-check the worst case (all on A4/A5) against 1024.

title: The "pairing rule" test does not exercise the pairing logic
description: The file header and the comment at line 97 say the pairing rule (Flight::start_mag_sample) is tested. The block only decodes two pages with seq 200 and 201 and compares them with a constant. The page-0 re-read on a seq mismatch, aru_imu_paired_, and IMU_F_PAIRED in gen_att are in flight.cpp, which the host build excludes, so no test covers them.
failure_scenario: A regression that drops the page-0 re-read, or sets aru_imu_paired_ from the first page-0 read (r before r2), passes this test and every host test.
proposed_fix: Move the read-and-pair step into a pure helper (e.g. a template over a page-reader callback returning {r, imu, paired}) and test the cases seq equal, seq differs then re-read matches, and re-read differs again or fails. Otherwise, reword the test comment so it does not claim to cover the rule.
verifier_evidence: The test_sensor_bus.cpp header lists 'the pairing rule', and the block commented 'Pairing (Flight::start_mag_sample)' only decodes two pages with seq 200/201 and compares them with a constant 200. The page-0 re-read on a seq mismatch, aru_imu_paired_ and IMU_F_PAIRED live in flight.cpp, which the host Makefile excludes (FSW_HOST filter-out). A regression in that logic passes every host test.
verifier_fix_notes: Move the read-and-pair step into a pure helper (a template over a page-reader callback returning {r, imu, paired}) in attitude.h, and test: seq equal; seq differs then the re-read matches; the re-read differs again or fails. Otherwise reword the test comment and the header so they do not claim to cover the rule.

title: ImuStats only resets in gen_att(): the first ATT after SAFE/BOOT aggregates every window since boot and reports imu_nwin = 255 (saturated)
description: imu_stats_.add() runs at every 1 Hz sample in every mode (start_mag_sample), but imu_stats_.reset() is only called in gen_att() (flight.cpp:1869). ATT is off in BOOT and SAFE (kModeCadence datalink.cpp:277-278), and the spacecraft boots into SAFE and waits for the ground. ImuStats::windows() saturates at 255 (attitude.h:104) while n_ keeps counting, so the first ATT after the operator commands CRUISE/TEST has these values over the whole SAFE time (hours): vib_rms (RMS of all windows), the peaks (max over hours) and rate_mean. imu_nwin is 255 with no saturation marker. The ground presents these as 'window statistics over the ATT period' (docs/13 9.4; dashboard.html:2074 'Windows aggregated 255'), and gds.ImuHistory plots them as one point at that ATT's receive time. The motion state is 'moving' if anything moved at any time in SAFE.
failure_scenario: Boot, 2 h in SAFE (about 7200 windows read), then CRUISE. The first ATT (generated at once because last_gen_s_ is 0) has imu_nwin=255 instead of 60, rate_peak and vib_peak equal to the largest values seen during the 2 h, and rate_mean equal to the 2 h mean. The SCIENCE table shows 'Windows aggregated 255' and possibly 'moving'. The IMU chart point at that time stands for 2 h, not one ATT period.
proposed_fix: Reset imu_stats_ whenever ATT is not being generated: in tick_1hz, when the ATT period in force is 0, call imu_stats_.reset() (it keeps last_win_). Or cap the aggregation to the nominal ATT period, e.g. reset at set_mode(). On the ground, render imu_nwin == 255 as '>= 255 (saturated)'.
verifier_evidence: imu_stats_.add() runs in every mode at each 1 Hz sample (flight.cpp:2290, inside the ARU poll started from service_mag/start_mag_sample, sample_due_ set unconditionally in tick_1hz :1580). imu_stats_.reset() is called only in gen_att() (:1869). ATT is 0 in BOOT and SAFE (datalink.cpp kModeCadence rows BOOT/SAFE). set_mode() zeroes last_gen_s_ (:1152), so the first ATT comes at once after CRUISE/TEST and aggregates everything since boot. windows() saturates at 255 (attitude.h:104) while n_ keeps counting. Host check (g++ out of tree, scratchpad/review31/verify-ICD/imu.cpp): 7200 windows with one 900 mg / 120 deg/s bump at t=100 s and rate 3 deg/s in the first hour give windows=255, vib_peak=900, rate_peak=1200 (0.1 deg/s units), rate_mean_x=150 (1.5 deg/s, the 2 h mean). No doc mentions this (docs/05:163 '1 s IMU windows aggregated', docs/13 'over the ATT period'). The simulator copies the behaviour (sim.py _imu_stats: imu_win_end starts at 0, 'at most the newest 255 windows'). It follows the contract text ('reset in gen_att()'), but the result breaks the documented meaning. Downgraded to minor: it affects one ATT per entry into an ATT-on mode (also after hibernation or an ATT period override of 0), and the next ATT is correct.
verifier_fix_notes: Flight: in tick_1hz, after periods_in_force(per), call imu_stats_.reset() whenever the ATT period in force is 0 or the spacecraft is hibernating. reset() keeps last_win_, so de-duplication survives. The first ATT after the mode change then covers at most the last second, or 0 windows with STATS clear, which the ground already handles. Mirror this in sim.py (set imu_win_end = int(t) while ATT is off). Ground: render imu_nwin == 255 as '>= 255 (saturated)'. Document in docs/05 and docs/13 that the first ATT after a mode change covers only the time since ATT generation started.

title: IMU_F_ cross-check only checks bit contiguity, not that flight names map to IMU_FLAG_BITS positions
description: The loop takes only the sorted VALUES of the IMU_F_ enum and asserts that they are [1<<i for i in range(len(names))]. The names are never compared, so the flight ImuFlag order is not checked against dictionary.IMU_FLAG_BITS. Contrast SENSOR_BITS/FDIR_BITS two lines above, which compare names sorted by value. The integration vector (imu_flags == 0x67) and test_bit_and_bist_decoders check numbers or the dictionary alone, so a swapped pair (e.g. IMU_F_PAIRED = 0x02 and IMU_F_STATS = 0x04 in tlm_packets.h) passes every test while the dashboard labels the bits wrongly. The same gap exists for the MAG_F_/ATT_F_/ENV_F_/RF_F_ entries the new one was added to.
failure_scenario: Edit tlm_packets.h: IMU_F_STATS = 0x04, IMU_F_PAIRED = 0x02. test_flight_header_constants_match_dictionary still passes. On the ground, a period with windows but no pairing shows the badge 'PAIRED' and 'imu_nwin 0' handling uses the wrong bit.
proposed_fix: For each prefix: e = _enum(tlm, rf"\b{prefix}(\w+)\s*=\s*(0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+)"); assert [n for n, _ in sorted(e.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])] == names and sorted(e.values()) == [1 << i for i in range(len(names))].
verifier_evidence: test_cross_check.py:204-206 compares only sorted(_enum(...).values()) with [1<<i]; names are never compared, unlike FDIR_/SNS_ (:198-201). Mutation check (scratchpad/review31/verify-ICD/icd4.py): swapping IMU_F_STATS=0x04 and IMU_F_PAIRED=0x02 in a copy of tlm_packets.h still passes the existing check and fails a name check. The integration vector (:405, imu_flags == 0x67) cannot catch this swap because STATS and PAIRED are both set in 0x67. test_bit_and_bist_decoders (:658) checks only the dictionary. No current mismatch: IMU_F_, MAG_F_ and RF_F_ names equal the dictionary lists today. The proposed fix as written would fail at once for ATT_F_ (flight ACC/MAG vs dictionary ACCEL/BMM150) and ENV_F_ (PRESSURE/TH vs BARO/TEMP_RH).
verifier_fix_notes: Compare names in order for IMU_F_, MAG_F_ and RF_F_: `e = _enum(tlm, rf"\b{prefix}(\w+)\s*=\s*(0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+)"); assert [n for n, _ in sorted(e.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])] == names`, keeping the contiguity assert. For ATT_F_ and ENV_F_, give an explicit alias map in the test ({'ACC': 'ACCEL', 'MAG': 'BMM150'}, {'PRESSURE': 'BARO', 'TH': 'TEMP_RH'}) and compare through it, or rename one side.

title: ImuStats: an ARU restart is not flagged as IMU_F_GAP when the pre-first-window page is read
description: The guard for 'the ARU before its first window' (win_seq 0, n 0, no STATS/MISSED) sets last_win_ = 0 and returns before the gap check, whether or not a window was already seen. After a Nicla reset (watchdog, brownout, re-plug) the flight reads a page with win_seq 0 / n 0 within the first second. The next window, win_seq 1, is then 'consecutive'. The seconds of the outage are never marked as a gap, contrary to the header comment ('a counter that moved backwards - an ARU restart - also shows as a gap'). Related doc slip: nicla_sense_me_aru.ino:58 and attitude.h:75 say 'win_seq 0 = none completed yet', but the counter wraps 255 -> 0 every 256 s.
failure_scenario: Host check (compiled into the scratch directory): add windows 130..137, reset(), then add(win_seq 0, n 0, flags 0) and add(win_seq 1, n 25, STATS). Result: gap()=0, windows()=1. The ATT says no windows were missed although the ARU was down for several seconds.
proposed_fix: In the guard, set gap_ = true when seen_ && last_win_ != 0 (the counter went back to the pre-window state), or keep the gap check before the guard. Fix the '0 = none completed yet' comments to say that win_seq 0 also follows 255.
verifier_evidence: attitude.cpp:184-188: the pre-first-window guard (win_seq 0, n 0, no STATS/MISSED) sets last_win_ = 0 and returns before the gap check at :191, whether or not a window had been seen. The Nicla firmware publishes that page for about 1 s after every restart: g_win starts at seq 0/n 0/flags 0, g_win_t0 = millis() right after Wire.begin, and pages are rebuilt at 10 Hz from the first loop pass (nicla_sense_me_aru.ino:189-197, 339-342, 390-405). The 1 Hz flight read will usually land in that second. Host check (scratchpad/review31/verify-ICD/imu.cpp): windows 130..137, reset(), add(0,n0,0), add(1,n25,STATS) give gap=0, windows=1. Control without the pre-window page gives gap=1. An outage shorter than 6 reads raises no 0x0606, so it leaves no trace in ATT, against the header comment. Doc slip confirmed: w.seq = g_win.seq + 1 wraps 255 -> 0 (ino:264), so 'win_seq 0 = none completed yet' (ino:58, attitude.h:75) is misleading. The wrap itself is handled (254,255,0,1 give gap=0, windows=4, because a real window 0 has n=25 and STATS, and n<23 sets MISSED).
verifier_fix_notes: In the guard: `if (seen_ && last_win_ != 0) gap_ = true;` before `last_win_ = 0`. The ARU went back to its pre-window state, i.e. it restarted. The first-ever reading (seen_ false) stays gap-free. Reword the comments: 'win_seq 0 with n 0 and no STATS/MISSED = no window completed since the ARU started; win_seq also reaches 0 after 255'. Add the host test sequence above.

title: IMU_F_PAIRED also requires a valid 9-DOF quaternion, so the ground's linear acceleration is withheld with a false reason
description: The flight sets IMU_F_PAIRED only when page-2 seq == page-0 seq AND aru_last_.motion_flags b0 (rotation vector valid). The ground gates the linear acceleration (acc - 1 g x u, which needs only q_grv and the page-0 accelerometer) on PAIRED. When q_fus is invalid but acc and q_grv come from the same rebuild, sensors.py:224 reports 'IMU_F_PAIRED clear: acc and q_grv not from one ARU rebuild', which is false. The tlm_packets.h comment and docs/05 define PAIRED purely as 'same ARU rebuild'.
failure_scenario: The 9-DOF rotation vector goes stale or fails the norm gate (ATT b0 QUAT clear) while GRV and the accelerometer are valid and paired by seq. The SCIENCE row shows 'n/a (IMU_F_PAIRED clear: acc and q_grv not from one ARU rebuild)' although they are from one rebuild, and the linear acceleration is not shown.
proposed_fix: Set IMU_F_PAIRED from aru_imu_paired_ && aru_valid_ alone; the ground already checks ATT b0 QUAT separately for the heading offset (sensors.py:226) and b1 ACCEL for the linear acceleration.
verifier_evidence: flight.cpp:1857: `if (aru_imu_paired_ && aru_valid_ && (aru_last_.motion_flags & 1u)) p.imu_flags |= IMU_F_PAIRED;`. motion_flags b0 is exactly what sets ATT_F_QUAT in the same ATT (:1817-1818), so PAIRED implies QUAT. tlm_packets.h:135, R3 line 695 and the contract define PAIRED as same ARU rebuild (page 2 seq = page 0 seq) only. Ground sensors.py:222-224: with PAIRED clear it sets na.lin_acc = 'IMU_F_PAIRED clear: acc and q_grv not from one ARU rebuild', and lin_acc needs only q_grv plus ATT b1 ACCEL. So when the 9-DOF rotation vector is stale or fails the norm gate while GRV and acc are paired by seq, the linear acceleration is withheld with a false reason. The ground's own 'ATT b0 QUAT clear: no valid 9-DOF rotation vector' branch (:227) can never be reached. aru_valid_ is implied by aru_imu_valid_ in the same poll, so dropping the b0 term is safe.
verifier_fix_notes: Set IMU_F_PAIRED from `aru_imu_paired_ && aru_valid_` (drop the motion_flags b0 term), keeping it inside the GRV-valid branch. The ground already gates the heading offset on ATT b0 QUAT and lin_acc on ATT b1 ACCEL. Add a flight host or vector case with QUAT clear and PAIRED set, and a ground test that lin_acc is produced and na.pair says 'ATT b0 QUAT clear'.
